requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1.
requirements.summary: A 2 GiB LUKS2 container was created with a root-owned mode-0600 key, opened as /dev/mapper/secure-volume, formatted with XFS, and directly observed mounted at /srv/secure before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The encrypted volume must unlock and mount automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: Persistent crypttab and fstab entries were installed. Automatic activation was first demonstrated from a closed mapper, then a real reboot changed the boot identity and the recovered system showed both crypto and mount units active, the filesystem mounted, and the persisted data checksum intact.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The system remained RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. Cryptsetup was installed from the configured RHEL 10 BaseOS repository, and final package-health observation succeeded.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a functioning LUKS2-backed XFS volume at /srv/secure, and a directly observed reboot demonstrated automatic unlock, automatic mounting, data persistence, and clean recovery while preserving the original RHEL release and kernel. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot identities.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, encrypted-container/key creation, filesystem creation, persistent configuration, and reboot were necessary implementation steps. The temporary stop/close/start operations were bounded functional verification; cmd-56d4dc8e54294c06 left the mount temporarily stopped after its check exited early, and cmd-57f78f1e143744c8 immediately performed the complete validation and restored the active mount. The transient reboot unit was held under /run and disappeared through reboot. Final observations show no failed services, no new listening exposure, healthy package state, and only normal reboot-generated temporary-directory turnover.
